headline: High-risk default interaction: Langflow can ingest and act on Haystack outputs via MCP/files, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes MCP servers and REST APIs, so its outputs can be fed into Langflow flows. Langflow accepts files and arbitrary HTTP/tool nodes, and its graph-based flows can chain agents. That creates a default pathway where Haystack-produced content can be treated as instructions by Langflow, with no provenance guard documented in either profile.
conditions: IF Haystack output is routed into a Langflow node that parses text as instructions
IF Langflow flow nodes consume uploaded files or API responses without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable direct ingestion of Haystack outputs into instruction-bearing nodes
Add a provenance tag and reject untrusted text at flow entry
Route Haystack output through a sanitizer/allowlist step
Turn off MCP exposure for the Haystack deployment
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing in Langflow

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can call REST/MCP endpoints, while Langflow reads and writes server filesystem data and stores per-flow credentials. If Haystack processes sensitive flow inputs or intermediate outputs from Langflow, those contents can be transmitted outward. The profiles do not show PHI or secrets, so this is leakage of workflow data rather than a critical breach.
conditions: IF Langflow uploads files or secrets into a flow that Haystack can query
IF Haystack forwards retrieved content to external APIs or MCP endpoints
mitigations: Restrict Haystack egress to approved domains
Store Langflow credentials outside shared flow inputs
Separate sensitive files from Haystack-accessible workspaces
Review flow logs for embedded secrets
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on flow outputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack can use MCP and broad network egress, while Langflow can execute shell, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. Even without shared write access, the pair can contend over shared server-side state or files if deployed together. The profiles do not prove a common directory, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed against the same server-side workspace or store
IF Langflow shell components and Haystack tools mutate the same external resource
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts and directories
Disable shell components in shared deployments
Serialize writes to shared stores
Use per-flow temporary workspaces
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack can emit retrieved facts through REST/MCP, and Langflow’s graph-based flows can chain multiple agents and tools. If Langflow treats Haystack output as authoritative, errors or prompt injections can cascade into downstream actions or generated artifacts. Because the profiles show no mandatory verification step, the unsafe path is plausible by default.
conditions: IF Langflow uses Haystack output as a downstream prompt or tool input
IF no verification or human review step is inserted between the agents
mitigations: Insert a verification node before any action-taking step
Require citations or source IDs from Haystack outputs
Limit Langflow tools to read-only actions
Add human approval for downstream side effects
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating between flow stages

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile. Haystack only lists anonymous usage statistics, while Langflow stores per-flow credentials and intermediate outputs. The main compliance concern is local policy alignment, not a proven cross-border or regulated-data violation, so the pairwise compliance risk remains low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Langflow flows that Haystack can access
IF deployment policy requires stricter retention than Langflow's flow-store behavior
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared flows
Document retention for flow inputs and outputs
Separate credential storage from retrievable artifacts
Review deployment region settings
requires-engineering: add policy-based retention controls
